title: [web][a11y] Reset scroll offsets when a list stops scrolling

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: a: accessibility
labels.description: Accessibility, e.g. VoiceOver or TalkBack. (aka a11y)

labels.name: f: scrolling
labels.description: Viewports, list views, slivers, etc.

labels.name: platform-web
labels.description: Web applications specifically

labels.name: team-web
labels.description: Owned by Web platform team

body:
<!--
Thanks for filing a pull request!
Reviewers are typically assigned within a week of filing a request.
To learn more about code review, see our documentation on Tree Hygiene: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/contributing/Tree-hygiene.md
-->

When a scrollable node's content shrinks until it fits the viewport (for example when list items are removed after scrolling), the framework drops the scroll actions and the node stops being scrollable. `SemanticScrollable.update()` then removed the overflow element and the scroll listeners but returned early — leaving `element.scrollTop`/`scrollLeft`, the memoized DOM scroll position, and the child-position scroll adjustments at their stale values.

The browser clamps `element.scrollTop` to the new (smaller) scroll range, but `verticalScrollAdjustment`/`horizontalScrollAdjustment` keep the last scrolled offset. Semantic child elements therefore stay shifted by `staleAdjustment - clampedScrollTop` pixels from the painted content, and DOM hit tests — including clicks and screen reader hit tests — land on the wrong nodes. In the issue's repro (20 rows x 40px in a 400px viewport, scroll 300px, shrink to 8 rows) the offset is 80px and tapping painted Row 4 activates Row 2.

This change registers a post-update callback on the non-scrollable path that resets the DOM scroll offsets and the scroll adjustments (via a `_resetScrollOffsets()` helper shared with the non-scrolling branch of `_updateScrollableState`, which already performed the same resets) and then recomputes the children's positions — mirroring what the scrollable path's callback does. The root cause was diagnosed by @aerotech-vadb in the issue report.

Two regression tests are added to `test/engine/semantics/scrollable_test.dart`, covering vertical and horizontal scrolling. Both build a real scrollable semantics node with positioned children, drive an actual DOM scroll offset, then shrink the content until the node loses its scroll actions, and assert that the adjustment and the DOM scroll offset are cleared — and that `document.elementFromPoint` at the painted row/column position resolves to the correct node rather than a stale-offset sibling. Both tests fail on unmodified code (`Expected: <0> / Actual: <300>` for the stale adjustment).

Verified locally with `felt` on Windows against `--gcs-prod` artifacts matching the base revision:

- `chrome-dart2js-canvaskit-engine`, all 12 `test/engine/semantics` files: 279/279 tests passed (1 skipped).
- `chrome-dart2wasm-canvaskit-engine`, `scrollable_test.dart` + `semantics_test.dart`: all 191 tests passed.
- `dart analyze` and `dart format` clean on the changed files; `git diff --check` clean.

Limitations: tested in Chrome with the CanvasKit renderer only (the engine test-set has no skwasm suite in `felt_config.yaml`); Skia Gold screenshot checks were skipped locally; verified at the engine DOM level (`elementFromPoint`), not with a live screen reader. Upstream CI has not run yet.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/195469

title: Fix TextField context menu after focus returns with unchanged selection

labels.name: a: text input
labels.description: Entering text in a text field or keyboard related problems

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

body:
## Description

Fixes #195408.

On Android, long-pressing an already selected word after dismissing a dialog can fail to reopen the TextField context menu.

The issue occurs because `EditableTextState.userUpdateTextEditingValue` returns early when the selection remains unchanged, skipping the long-press selection update needed to recreate the selection overlay after focus returns.

### Changes

- Allow repeated long presses to reach the existing selection-update path even when the `TextEditingValue` is unchanged.
- Preserve the existing early-return behavior for other unchanged interactions.
- Add an Android widget regression test covering dialog dismissal, focus restoration, and repeated long press.

title: Flutter SDK upgrade requires PowerShell, which is restricted in Banking Network (Windows)

labels.name: waiting for response
labels.description: The Flutter team cannot make further progress on this issue until the original reporter responds

body:
We are facing an issue while upgrading to the latest Flutter SDK on Windows machines.
Our organization works in a restricted banking network environment, and due to security policies, PowerShell access is completely blocked for all employees.

The latest Flutter SDK on Windows requires PowerShell to run critical setup commands (including flutter doctor, flutter upgrade, SDK initialization scripts etc.). Since PowerShell is mandatory, the SDK upgrade does not proceed and errors are thrown.

As we cannot enable PowerShell due to strict banking security policies, we are completely unable to update Flutter SDK to the latest stable release.

**Environment Details**
OS: Windows (Enterprise / Banking Restricted Environment)
PowerShell: Not available (blocked by IT security policy)
Terminal availability: Only CMD is allowed
Flutter version: Older version (works fine without PowerShell)
Need: A way to upgrade Flutter SDK without requiring PowerShell, or an alternative shell compatibility option.

Run a Flutter application on a Windows PC equipped with an Intel Core Ultra 5 125H or Intel Core Ultra 7 155H processor and its integrated GPU.

Monitor the application's memory usage in Windows Task Manager while it is running.

Run the same Flutter application on systems equipped with an NVIDIA discrete GPU, an older Intel integrated GPU, and an Intel Arc B580 discrete GPU, and compare the memory usage.

### Expected results

Memory usage should remain within a reasonable range when running the same Flutter application under similar conditions across different GPU configurations. There should not be a significant unexplained difference in memory usage on specific integrated GPUs.

title: [Linux] Fix stuck modifier when two keys are pressed as the same modifier

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: platform-linux
labels.description: Building on or for Linux specifically

labels.name: a: desktop
labels.description: Running on desktop

labels.name: team-linux
labels.description: Owned by the Linux platform team

body:
When a modifier bit is cleared, the Linux embedder released the physical key from the last key-down mapping instead of the key that is actually pressed. If two keys produce the same logical key (e.g. CapsLock remapped to Control plus the real Control) and a release is missed, it sent an up event with logical key 0, hit the `update_pressing_state` assertion, and Control stayed stuck.

This releases every physical key recorded as pressed for that logical key, and fixes `reverse_lookup_hash_table`, which returned the value instead of the key.

Two new tests in `fl_key_embedder_responder_test.cc` fail without the fix and pass with it. I couldn't reproduce the reporters' exact setups, but this is the only path that produces both errors in their logs.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/150326

title: [web][a11y] Initialize slider semantics values when enabling

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: a: accessibility
labels.description: Accessibility, e.g. VoiceOver or TalkBack. (aka a11y)

labels.name: platform-web
labels.description: Web applications specifically

labels.name: team-web
labels.description: Owned by Web platform team

body:
<!--
Thanks for filing a pull request!
Reviewers are typically assigned within a week of filing a request.
To learn more about code review, see our documentation on Tree Hygiene: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/contributing/Tree-hygiene.md
-->

When a `Slider` is enabled after its semantics node already exists, the web engine attaches a new `SemanticIncrementable` role to a node whose `value`, `increasedValue`, and `decreasedValue` fields are not dirty. `_updateInputValues()` then returns early on the role's first `update()`, so the hidden `<input type="range">` is exposed to assistive technology without `value`, `min`, `max`, `aria-valuetext`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, or `aria-valuemax`. The browser announces the default range value ("50") until the slider's value changes once.

This change starts `_pendingResync` as `true`, so a newly attached role performs one initial input-value sync on its first `update()` — the approach proposed by @cashmula in the issue's "Likely cause" analysis, which also identified the root cause. The flag is cleared after that sync; its existing role in `change`-event handling is unchanged. `SemanticsNodeUpdate` normalizes absent value fields to empty strings, so the initial sync cannot hit null-asserts.

Three regression tests are added to `test/engine/semantics/semantics_test.dart`: enabling a previously disabled slider with unchanged values (the reported bug), disabling and re-enabling a slider (role reattachment resync), and role attachment while the engine is in pointer-events gesture mode (input stays disabled but attributes still sync).

The first test fails on unmodified code: the input renders as bare `<input type="range" role="slider" tabindex="0">` with `value="50"`.

Verified locally with `felt` on Windows against `--gcs-prod` artifacts matching the base revision:

- `chrome-dart2js-canvaskit-engine`, all 12 `test/engine/semantics` files: 280/280 tests passed.
- `chrome-dart2wasm-canvaskit-engine`, `semantics_test.dart`: all 191 tests passed.

title: Rebuild EditableText when it regains focus with a valid selection

labels.name: a: text input
labels.description: Entering text in a text field or keyboard related problems

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

labels.name: f: focus
labels.description: Focus traversal, gaining or losing focus

body:
When an `EditableText` regains focus and its selection is already valid (for example, collapsed at the end from a previous focus), `_handleFocusChanged` never rebuilds the widget. `_Editable` passes `hasFocus` to `RenderEditable` from `build`, so `RenderEditable.hasFocus` and the semantics `isFocused` flag stay `false` while `FocusNode.hasFocus` is `true`.

On web with semantics enabled, this drops input: the engine activates semantics text editing only for a text field whose node reports focus. `TextField` and `CupertinoTextField` hide the bug because they rebuild on every focus change themselves.

This change calls `setState` on every focus change, not only on focus loss. `_currentPromptRectRange` is still only cleared when focus is lost.

Fixes #195407

## Tests

title: Predictive back is modeled as a per-page transition builder, which cannot coordinate route pairs or nested navigators

labels.name: platform-android
labels.description: Android applications specifically

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

labels.name: f: routes
labels.description: Navigator, Router, and related APIs.

labels.name: c: proposal
labels.description: A detailed proposal for a change to Flutter

labels.name: team-framework
labels.description: Owned by Framework team

body:
## Summary

Several issues in Flutter's predictive back support look like isolated edge cases at first glance, but actually stem from the same architectural mismatch:

1. **Unrelated gestures trigger predictive back visuals (#187492):** Dragging a `CupertinoSheet` over a page that uses `PredictiveBackPageTransitionsBuilder` or `PredictiveBackFullscreenPageTransitionsBuilder` causes the underlying page to jump into the predictive back transition and clip its corners. The narrower condition proposed in flutter/packages#12705 still reproduces ([repro comment link](TODO)).
2. **Mixed routes cannot animate together:** When a Material page using a predictive back builder is popped over a `CupertinoPageRoute` (or a custom route), the revealed page remains frozen instead of animating with the predictive back gesture, because the predictive back builders return `null` for `delegatedTransition` and the revealed route does not run the predictive transition itself.
3. **Nested navigators pop the wrong route or pop multiple routes at once (#152323 and its duplicates #183597, #185444):** Swiping back while a root dialog or page covers a nested `Navigator` pops the hidden nested route underneath (#152323); and when both parent and child navigators have active routes, a single back swipe pops both simultaneously (#183597, #185444).

These are not bugs caused by a missing boolean check. They happen because **predictive back is modeled as a per-route `PageTransitionsBuilder` with a per-route global `WidgetsBindingObserver`**, whereas the feature being modeled is a **navigator-level interaction that must follow the same dispatch path as back presses and choreograph a pair of routes**.

## Why these bugs prove the current model is wrong

### 1. A two-page choreography is split across two independent `PageTransitionsBuilder`s
During an Android predictive back gesture, the exiting top page and the revealed page beneath it move as a single coordinated animation. Under the current model, nobody owns that pair: `PageTransitionsBuilder.buildTransitions` runs independently for each route, and each page is responsible for switching its own subtree from its standard transition (`FadeForwards` or `Zoom`) to the predictive transition.

Because the exiting page handles the gesture while the revealed page declines it, **the revealed page has no direct way to know what the page on top is doing.** It is forced to guess by reading indirect signals:
- **`route.popGestureInProgress` is navigator-wide, not route-specific:** Despite its doc comment, it returns `navigator!.userGestureInProgress`, which is true during *any* user gesture on the navigator—including a `CupertinoSheet` drag or an iOS back swipe.
- **Local observer `_phase` goes stale whenever a gesture is declined:** Every `_PredictiveBackGestureDetector` sets `_phase = start` when `handleStartBackGesture` arrives, before checking whether to accept it. Detectors that decline the gesture never receive `commit` or `cancel`, leaving `_phase` stuck at `start` indefinitely.

Any attempt to fix this while keeping per-route inference runs into a wall:
- **Only setting `_phase` when accepting** breaks the revealed page, which declines the gesture and would never enter the predictive transition. Moreover, `WidgetsBindingObserver`s run in registration order, so the revealed page receives `handleStartBackGesture` *before* the top page even decides whether to accept it.
- **Scoping `popGestureInProgress` to the route directly above** still fails because dragging a `CupertinoSheet` *is* that sheet route's pop gesture—and existing consumers like `CupertinoPageTransitionsBuilder` rely on `popGestureInProgress` being navigator-wide.
- **Wiring a detector into `delegatedTransition` (in-flight PR #174337)** still relies on the same per-route inference: the revealed route wraps itself in its own detector and checks `_phase` and `route?.popGestureInProgress` to guess whether a predictive back gesture is underway, while `delegatedTransition` itself is wired up when the route stack changes rather than per gesture and receives the revealed route's animations rather than the top route's state.
- **Broadcasting a navigator-level "predictive back in progress" flag** only works when both routes understand the broadcast. If a Material page is popped to reveal a `CupertinoPageRoute` or custom route that doesn't read the flag, the revealed route still cannot participate properly.

### 2. Gesture dispatch is split from back-press dispatch and bypasses the `Navigator` hierarchy
On Android (`OnBackInvokedDispatcher` / `OnBackPressedDispatcher`), a discrete back button press and a continuous predictive back gesture are routed through the same dispatcher: a single active callback is selected at start time based on priority and enabled state, and only that callback receives the gesture lifecycle (`started` -> `progressed` -> `committed`/`cancelled`).

In Flutter, discrete back presses go through `handlePopRoute` -> `WidgetsApp` / `Router` -> root `Navigator.maybePop`, delegating to nested navigators only when explicitly forwarded via `NavigatorPopHandler` or `ChildBackButtonDispatcher`. Predictive back gestures ignore that path completely. Because `_PredictiveBackGestureDetector` lives inside `PageTransitionsBuilder`, every page registers its own global `WidgetsBindingObserver` and checks `route.isCurrent && route.popGestureEnabled` in isolation:
- `route.isCurrent` only means "on top of my own `Navigator`". A route inside a nested `Navigator` has no idea that its enclosing route in the root `Navigator` is covered by a `Dialog` or another page (#152323).
- Since #154718, `WidgetsBinding` sends `update` and `commit` to *every* observer that returns `true` from `handleStartBackGesture` (contradicting the method's doc comment). When both a parent and child navigator have `isCurrent` routes with predictive back builders (and the parent is not blocked by a `PopScope`), both accept the gesture and both pop (#152323, #183597, #185444).

### 3. Forward transitions and predictive back transitions are artificially coupled
Embedding predictive back inside `PageTransitionsBuilder` forces apps to pick a builder (`PredictiveBackPageTransitionsBuilder` or `PredictiveBackFullscreenPageTransitionsBuilder`) that hardcodes a specific forward transition (`FadeForwards` or `Zoom`), and leaves `CupertinoPageRoute` unable to participate in predictive back on Android at all.

## Requirements that any replacement model must meet

To fix these issues at the root rather than trading one edge case for another, the model needs to satisfy:

1. **Unified, single-target dispatch aligned with back presses:** At most one `Navigator` and one `Route` may handle a system back gesture, chosen at gesture start using the same hierarchy and explicit forwarding rules (`NavigatorPopHandler` / `BackButtonDispatcher`) as standard back presses (#152323).
2. **Single-owner two-page choreography:** Within the handling navigator, the exiting route must drive both its own exit transition and the revealed route's entrance transition during a predictive back gesture—without the revealed route inspecting gesture signals, and regardless of what `PageTransitionsBuilder` or `ModalRoute` subclass the revealed page uses (#187492).
3. **Gesture isolation until settle:** Predictive back visuals must trigger *only* for accepted system back gestures (never for sheet drags or iOS back swipes), and must remain active after `commit` or `cancel` until the route's settle animation finishes.
4. **Surface-specific participation:** A route being popped must be able to choose whether to use the two-page predictive transition (standard pages), drive its own primary animation directly (e.g., container transforms), or opt out (e.g., dialogs and sheets).
5. **Decoupling from forward transitions and `material_ui`:** Predictive back configuration should be independent of the forward `PageTransitionsBuilder` and live at the `widgets` layer so `CupertinoPageRoute` and custom `ModalRoute`s can participate on Android.
6. **Backward compatibility:** Existing `PageTransitionsBuilder`s, custom `Route` subclasses, and `go_router` setups must keep working without breaking changes unless an app opts in.

*(See the follow-up comment for a concrete design sketch and incremental migration path.)*

title: Support a shared storage location for compatible libflutter.so files to reduce disk usage

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: c: proposal
labels.description: A detailed proposal for a change to Flutter

labels.name: team-engine
labels.description: Owned by Engine team

body:
### Use case

I am seeing many copies of `libflutter.so` on my device. These files are large, and keeping multiple copies takes up a significant amount of disk space.

I would like a way to avoid storing redundant copies of the same Flutter engine library.

### Proposal

Could Flutter support an optional common storage location for `libflutter.so`, allowing projects or applications to reuse a single compatible copy instead of each keeping its own?

Sharing should only apply when the engine version, target architecture, and build mode are compatible. Different or incompatible engine binaries should remain separate.

The goal is to reduce disk usage caused by duplicate Flutter engine libraries. If sharing across installed Android applications is restricted by platform security or packaging requirements, could Flutter provide a supported deduplication mechanism for local development and build artifacts instead?

I do not have a specific implementation in mind; I would appreciate guidance on whether this could be supported and what platform constraints would apply.

title: [cupertino_ui] Dropdown support: official widget planned, or expose menu surface customization?

labels.name: p: cupertino_ui
labels.description: cupertino_ui package in flutter/packages

labels.name: package
labels.description: flutter/packages repository. See also p: labels.

labels.name: c: proposal
labels.description: A detailed proposal for a change to Flutter

labels.name: team-design
labels.description: Owned by Design Languages team

body:
### Use case

`cupertino_ui` has no dropdown / pull-down button widget. Material has `DropdownButton`,
`DropdownMenu` and `DropdownMenuFormField`; Cupertino has `CupertinoSegmentedControl` for
small choice sets, and `CupertinoMenuAnchor` plus `CupertinoMenuItem` for menus, but nothing
that represents a *field showing the selected value that opens a menu of choices*.

Pull-down menus did land (issue #60298 was closed as completed, implemented by
`CupertinoMenuAnchor`), so the menu surface exists. What is missing is the trigger/field part:
on iOS a pull-down button is a label plus chevron whose fill ramps with the open state, whose
menu matches the button width, and which marks the selected item with a checkmark. Today every
app that needs a Cupertino-style dropdown has to re-create that button and its open/close state
on top of `CupertinoMenuAnchor`, and there is no way to style the menu panel itself.

`CupertinoMenuItem` is flexible enough for the item side (`leading` / `trailing` / `decoration` /
`isDestructiveAction`), so a hand-rolled dropdown gets most of the way there. The blocker is the
panel: its background color, corner radius, blur, shadow and width are fixed to the iOS 17/18
reference values with no public hook.

Concrete limitations in `cupertino_ui` 1.1.4, taken from the package source:

- `CupertinoMenuAnchor` exposes 15 parameters (`controller`, `onOpen`, `onClose`,
  `onAnimationStatusChanged`, `constraints`, `constrainCrossAxis`, `consumeOutsideTaps`,
  `enableSwipe`, `enableLongPressToOpen`, `useRootOverlay`, `overlayPadding`, `menuChildren`,
  `builder`, `child`, `childFocusNode`). None of them affects the menu surface, and panel size
  can only be influenced indirectly through `constraints`.
- The panel is built inside the private `_MenuOverlay`, which always wraps the content in
  `CupertinoPopupSurface()`. `CupertinoMenuAnchor` does not accept an `overlayBuilder`, so its
  private layout/animation/swipe/focus logic cannot be reused with a different surface.
- `CupertinoPopupSurface` only exposes `blurSigma` and `isSurfacePainted`. The surface color is
  the private constant `_kDialogColor` (`0xCCF2F2F2` light / `0xCC2D2D2D` dark).
- The shadow is painted by the private `_ShadowPainter` with fixed constants (corner radius 13,
  opacity 0.12, blur up to sigma 50, color `RGBO(0, 0, 10)`). There is no configuration path, and
  its `brightness` field is not actually used in `paint`, so light and dark shadows are identical.
- The menu width comes from content plus `constraints`. There is no way to match the trigger
  width, which is the default pull-down-button behavior on iOS. (#188853 asks for positioning
  control, which is related but a different gap.)

Why this matters beyond pure iOS fidelity: this app targets iOS, macOS, Android, Windows and
Linux from a single Cupertino-styled widget tree with an app-level brand color. A menu panel
hard-coded to `#F2F2F2 @ 80%` over a blurred backdrop does not blend with a branded surface, and
the fidelity defaults are also iOS-specific in ways a cross-platform app may want to relax (for
example, less blur on desktop).

The only current ways out are (a) fork `cupertino_ui`, or (b) rebuild the overlay on top of
`RawMenuAnchor` and lose the open/close spring, the decoy-child preview animation, the
`_MenuLayoutDelegate` positioning and flip, swipe-to-select, focus/`Actions`/`Shortcuts`
traversal and `TapRegion` dismissal (roughly 600 lines of behavior). We evaluated both. Neither
is maintainable for a visual-only difference, and we would rather not ship a fork.

Current hand-rolled dropdown, for context:

```dart
CupertinoMenuAnchor(
  menuChildren: [
    for (final item in items)
      CupertinoMenuItem(
        leading: item == value
            ? Icon(CupertinoIcons.check_mark, size: fontSize, color: labelColor)
            : null,
        onPressed: () => onChanged?.call(item),
        child: Text(item.label, style: textTheme.textStyle),
      ),
  ],
  builder: (context, controller, child) => CupertinoButton(
    color: isHovered ? hoverColor : null,
    onPressed: () => controller.isOpen ? controller.close() : controller.open(),
    child: child!,
  ),
  child: Row(
    mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
    children: [
      Text(value.label, style: textTheme.textStyle),
      const SizedBox(width: 4),
      Icon(CupertinoIcons.chevron_up_chevron_down, color: labelColor),
    ],
  ),
)
```

### Proposal

Two questions; either answer unblocks us.

1. **Is an official Cupertino dropdown / pull-down button widget planned?** If it is on the
   roadmap (for example as part of the iOS 26 work tracked in #170310), please point us at the
   tracking issue and we will wait for it instead of asking for customization hooks.

2. **If it is not planned, would you accept opt-in customization on `CupertinoMenuAnchor`?**
   All defaults would stay exactly as they are, so the iOS-fidelity path is untouched. In rough
   priority order for building a dropdown:

   - A style or builder for the panel — one of: `menuSurfaceBuilder`, `menuDecoration`, or a
     `CupertinoMenuStyle` / `CupertinoMenuThemeData` (theme-level and `ThemeExtension`-friendly)
     covering `backgroundColor`, `borderRadius`, `blurSigma` and `shadow` (color, opacity, blur,
     offset). Defaults equal today's values.
   - `matchAnchorWidth` (or an explicit width / `minWidth` derived from the anchor's `RenderBox`),
     which is what a pull-down button needs.
   - `blurSigma` passthrough to the internal `CupertinoPopupSurface`, so glass strength can be
     tuned per platform.
   - A public `overlayBuilder` escape hatch, similar to `RawMenuAnchor`'s, that still receives the
     resolved `anchorRect`, `overlaySize`, `tapRegionGroupId` and `focusScopeNode`. That would let
     an app supply its own surface while keeping the stock animation, gesture and layout logic.
   - Menu open progress (`Animation<double>`) in the `builder`, so a trigger can render its fill
     ramp while the menu opens instead of only reacting to `AnimationStatus` transitions.

   We are glad to send a PR for whichever subset you consider acceptable in shape. Please let us
   know the API you would prefer — individual parameters or a `CupertinoMenuStyle` — and we can
   draft it. Our own constraint is that the defaults must stay pixel-identical to the current
   iOS reference behavior.

body:
Revealing a focused text field can scroll the inner list while the sheet is partially expanded. Subsequent upward drags then keep scrolling the list.

Prioritize expanding the sheet on upward drags and returning the list to its start before shrinking on downward drags. Transfer remaining drag distance across boundaries while respecting scroll physics and activity changes.

Add regression coverage for keyboard appearance and dismissal, programmatic scrolling, boundary transitions, and gesture cancellation.

Here is what the behavior looked like before and after these changes:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f294cc7-234d-4493-82c4-2acb520b8b7b

And before/after with max 0.6:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df952b49-10a6-4bab-a92f-b52fe7c37db0

Fixes #94942

body:
<!--
Thanks for filing a pull request!
Reviewers are typically assigned within a week of filing a request.
To learn more about code review, see our documentation on Tree Hygiene: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/contributing/Tree-hygiene.md
-->

Removes the unexplained file-level `@TestOn('!chrome')` annotations from two widget test files so they also run on the web:

- `packages/flutter/test/widgets/accessibility_inspector_test.dart`: every test passes on Chrome with both CanvasKit (dart2js) and Skwasm (dart2wasm).
- `packages/flutter/test/widgets/color_filter_test.dart`: four of the five tests pass on Chrome with both CanvasKit and Skwasm. The `color_filter_red.png` and `color_filter_saturation.png` goldens match the Linux baselines. The `Color filter - sepia` golden test is still skipped on web (`skip: kIsWeb`, with a comment saying why). Its `Text` widgets have no color set, and the web engine draws text with no color in black, while native draws it white, so the golden comes out different.

Keeping the whole files skipped hid any web regressions in these tests.

No tracking issue: neither `@TestOn('!chrome')` annotation pointed to an issue, and this is a test-only change.

title: [web] Unify font collections between CanvasKit and Skwasm

labels.name: a: text input
labels.description: Entering text in a text field or keyboard related problems

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: platform-web
labels.description: Web applications specifically

labels.name: team-web
labels.description: Owned by Web platform team

body:
Part of https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/175630.

This moves font handling to the same `Engine*` -> `Backend*` layering that `Paragraph`, `Path`, `Shader` and `ImageFilter` already use. `EngineFontCollection` (shared by both renderers) now owns everything that used to be duplicated between `SkiaFontCollection` and `SkwasmFontCollection`: downloading asset fonts, the implicit Roboto default, the registered font bookkeeping, the fallback font registry and the `FontFallbackManager`.

`CkFontCollection` and `SkwasmFontCollection` only implement `BackendFontCollection`: parse bytes into a `BackendTypeface`, register a typeface under a family name, receive the fallback family list, and clear. `CkTypeface`/`SkwasmTypeface` implement `BackendTypeface` and expose the typeface's family name, which is what `loadFontFromBytes` uses when no family is given. Skwasm gets a new `typeface_getFamilyName` export for that.

`SkiaFontCollection`, `SkiaFallbackRegistry`, `SkwasmFallbackRegistry` and the CanvasKit-only `skia_font_collection_test.dart` are gone; the shared `font_collection_test.dart` covers the same cases for both renderers.

Behavior differences worth calling out:
- CanvasKit `clear()` now actually unregisters fonts (it was a no-op before).
- CanvasKit no longer rebuilds the whole `TypefaceFontProvider` on every registration; it registers incrementally and recreates the skparagraph `FontCollection` lazily, same as Skwasm's `clearCaches`.
- Skwasm now prints the same warnings as CanvasKit for missing/invalid fonts, and no longer mutates the caller's `FontManifest`.
- Registration order is deterministic (manifest order) on both renderers.
- `SkwasmFontCollection.createTypeface` checks for a null typeface before wrapping it, so an invalid font no longer disposes a null handle.

title: Replace pull_request_target workflows with pull_request + workflow_run

labels.name: CICD
labels.description: Run CI/CD

body:
This resolves https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/193185.

GitHub is restricting `pull_request_target`, which runs with secrets and a write token on events from forks. Each affected workflow is split in two:

* An unprivileged `pull_request` workflow with a read-only token and no secrets. Cheap gates (label name, base branch, bot author) are job-level `if:`s so non-matching events never allocate a runner. When it applies, it uploads a small artifact with context about the triggering event (PR number, and the cp channel).

* A privileged `workflow_run` workflow that runs from the default branch with access to secrets. It downloads the artifact and does the actual work: commenting, labeling, reverting, cherry-picking, deleting branches.

A PR can modify the `pull_request` workflow, so the artifact is untrusted. The privileged side ties the PR number to the triggering run's head SHA and repo. It then reads all other state from the GitHub API, including re-checking any gate whose failure would have made the trigger skip. Checks that end in a comment either way are done only on the privileged side.

| Unprivileged (pull_request)     | Privileged (workflow_run) |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------|
| revert-trigger.yml              | revert.yml                |
| cp-trigger.yml                  | easy-cp.yml               |
| labeler-trigger.yml             | labeler.yml               |
| delete-bot-branches-trigger.yml | delete-bot-branches.yml   |
| freeze.yml                      | freeze-comment.yml        |
| no-main-prs.yaml                | no-main-prs-comment.yaml  |

freeze.yml and no-main-prs.yaml keep their names because they still provide the PR check. no-main-prs.yaml now gates on `base_ref == 'main'` at the job level, so it no longer uses a runner on every PR.

labels.description: Run CI/CD

body:
This is a proof of concept API change that replaces the `anchorRect` argument in `PopupWindowController` and `TooltipWindowController` with a `ValueGetter<Rect>`. 

This solves discrepancy where the controller itself is in charge of positioning the window (calling the positioner), but anchor rect needs to be "pushed" by somebody else to the controller every time it changes. By using `ValueGetter` the controller will request the anchor rect every time it needs it - and it does it in a well defined place in frame cycle when the layout is already settled.

In this PR the positioning is driven from Dart (through a `persistentFrameCallback`), which fixes another issue we were having - the position of tooltip/popup is dependent on the tooltip/popup being repainted. This will break as soon as we have individual view repaints. Instead the position is now updated on each frame, and the positioner for child windows is guaranteed to be called *after* parent window positioner.

### What package does this bug report belong to?

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

    dependency: "direct main"

      name: cupertino_ui

      url: "https://pub.dev"

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the widget test below.

### Expected results

VoiceOver reads a segment in `disabledChildren` as dimmed and offers no tap, like a disabled `UISegmentedControl` segment.

### Actual results

It looks dimmed, but has no enabled state, and a tap that does nothing. Each segment's `Semantics(button: true)` sets no `enabled`, and its `onTap` stays, only returning early.

Same in `CupertinoSegmentedControl`, on `main`, and in the framework's copies.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:cupertino_ui/cupertino_ui.dart';

void main() => runApp(
  CupertinoApp(
    home: Center(
      child: CupertinoSlidingSegmentedControl<int>(
        groupValue: 0,
        onValueChanged: (_) {},
        disabledChildren: const {1},
        children: const {0: Text('Photo'), 1: Text('Video')},
      ),
    ),
  ),
);
```

</details>

<details><summary>Widget test</summary>

```dart
import 'package:cupertino_ui/cupertino_ui.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

void main() {
  testWidgets('a disabled segment tells screen readers it is disabled', (tester) async {
    final semantics = tester.ensureSemantics();
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      CupertinoApp(
        home: Center(
          child: CupertinoSlidingSegmentedControl<int>(
            groupValue: 0,
            onValueChanged: (_) {},
            disabledChildren: const {1},
            children: const {0: Text('Photo'), 1: Text('Video')},
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );

    expect(
      tester.getSemantics(find.text('Video')),
      // Fails: no enabled state, and a tap.
      containsSemantics(isButton: true, hasEnabledState: true, isEnabled: false, hasTapAction: false),
    );
    semantics.dispose();
  });
}
```

`CupertinoSegmentedControl` in place of `CupertinoSlidingSegmentedControl` fails the same way.

</details>

title: [ios] Update the screen in didUpdateEffectiveGeometry

labels.name: platform-ios
labels.description: iOS applications specifically

labels.name: engine

labels.name: team-ios

body:
This is a follow up to https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/195199

As discussed [in this thread](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/195199#discussion_r4374608180), For a fixed-size FlutterView, `viewDidLayoutSubviews` is called when switching from outer to inner display, but not called when switching from inner to outer display. This is a puzzling behavior (possibly a bug in UIKit), but it does prove that relying on `viewDidLayoutSubviews` is not complete.

The only API we can find that triggers when a scene changes screen is `didUpdateEffectiveGeometry`. There won't be a breaking change, but it would require `FlutterSceneLifeCycleProvider` users to add a one-liner for this to work. We should update our website to include this ([PR](https://github.com/flutter/website/pull/14012)):  

```
func windowScene(_ windowScene: UIWindowScene,
                 didUpdateEffectiveGeometry previousEffectiveGeometry: UIWindowScene.Geometry) {
  sceneLifeCycleDelegate.windowScene(windowScene, didUpdateEffectiveGeometry: previousEffectiveGeometry)
}
```

## Testing

I have manually verified with a fixed-size 300x300 FlutterView, and confirmed the information is correctly updated when switching screen. 

It is not possible to write integration test - I don't think there's a `simctl` sub-command that allows us to fold/unfold the simulator. We could add a integration test in the future if such api become available.

But this doesn't discover new sync hazards. Enabling sync validation adds a lot of CPU cost, so I don't recommend we run our whole suite of engine tests with it enabled. Instead, I recommend we set up a new CI shard with vulkan sync validation enabled (VK_VALIDATION_VALIDATE_SYNC=1 or VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION_EXT) which covers a carefully selected set of impeller tests.

title: Preserve negative angles when interpolating sweep gradients

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

body:
Preserve negative angles when interpolating sweep gradients

SweepGradient accepts negative start and end angles, but lerp clamps both angles to zero. This changes valid gradients even at t = 0 or t = 1, and can collapse a negative-angle sweep to a zero-length sweep.

Interpolate the angles directly, as signed radians. Regression tests cover distinct gradients at both endpoints, interpolation through Gradient.lerp, and extrapolation from positive angles into negative angles.

Fixes #195470.

Validation on Windows:
- All 70 tests in gradient_test.dart, box_decoration_test.dart and shape_decoration_test.dart pass with coverage.
- All three new regression tests fail on the original production code.
- Coverage includes both modified angle expressions.
- Dart formatting and git diff --check pass.
- Static analysis passes with no issues.

The full Flutter suite has not run. Existing gradient rendering tests were included; no new screenshot comparison was added. No public API or documentation migration is required.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The contributor reviewed and approved this final diff and description before publication.

title: [iOS] Platform message handlers queued before destroyContext run after it and crash: "Setting a message handler before the FlutterEngine has been run"

labels.name: platform-ios
labels.description: iOS applications specifically

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: has reproducible steps
labels.description: The issue has been confirmed reproducible and is ready to work on

labels.name: team-ios
labels.description: Owned by iOS platform team

body:
### Steps to reproduce

On iOS, a platform message handler that Dart queued just before the engine is torn down runs after `destroyContext`. If that handler registers a channel, as `FlutterEventChannel setStreamHandler:` does for a Firestore `snapshots()` call, the app crashes with an `NSInternalInconsistencyException`.

Minimal native repro (any app; for example in `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:`):

```swift
let engine = FlutterEngine(name: "repro")
engine.run()
engine.perform(NSSelectorFromString("destroyContext"))  // what appOrSceneWillTerminate does
_ = engine.binaryMessenger.setMessageHandlerOnChannel("repro", binaryMessageHandler: { _, _ in })
```

The app terminates with `Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInternalInconsistencyException', reason: 'Setting a message handler before the FlutterEngine has been run.'`

### How it happens in production

1. `FlutterViewController sceneWillDisconnect:` (or `applicationWillTerminate:`) calls `appOrSceneWillTerminate`, which calls `[engine destroyContext]`, and that calls `_shell.reset()`.
2. `PlatformMessageHandlerIos::HandlePlatformMessage` runs each handler with `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), run_handler)` (or the handler's task queue), so a message Dart sent just before step 1 is already queued.
3. The queued handler runs after the teardown. The cloud_firestore pigeon `querySnapshot` handler calls `registerEventChannelWithPrefix:`, which calls `-[FlutterEventChannel setStreamHandler:]`, which calls `-[FlutterEngine setMessageHandlerOnChannel:binaryMessageHandler:taskQueue:]`, which reaches `NSAssert(!handler, @"Setting a message handler before the FlutterEngine has been run.")`.

`sendOnChannel:message:binaryReply:` has the same `NSAssert(_shell && _shell->IsSetup(), ...)`. Any native event sink that fires after the teardown reaches it; see flutter/flutter#117523 and the termination crashes in #126671, #167650 and #168535.

Production stack (iOS 27.0.1, Flutter 3.47.5, cloud_firestore 6.10.0; app in the background for hours, scene disconnected):

```
-[NSAssertionHandler handleFailureInMethod:object:file:lineNumber:description:]
-[FlutterEngine setMessageHandlerOnChannel:binaryMessageHandler:taskQueue:]
-[FlutterBinaryMessengerRelay setMessageHandlerOnChannel:binaryMessageHandler:]
SetMessageHandler
SetStreamHandlerMessageHandlerOnChannel
-[FlutterEventChannel setStreamHandler:]
-[FLTFirebaseFirestorePlugin registerEventChannelWithPrefix:identifier:streamHandler:]
-[FLTFirebaseFirestorePlugin registerEventChannelWithPrefix:streamHandler:]
-[FLTFirebaseFirestorePlugin querySnapshotApp:path:isCollectionGroup:parameters:options:includeMetadataChanges:source:completion:]
__SetUpFirebaseFirestoreHostApiWithSuffix_block_invoke
__48-[FlutterBasicMessageChannel setMessageHandler:]_block_invoke
```

### Expected results

Once the engine is torn down, setting a handler and sending a message should be no-ops, as setting a nil handler already is (`return [FlutterConnectionCollection makeErrorConnectionWithErrorCode:-1L]`), or queued handlers should be dropped when the shell is reset. A plugin cannot tell that the engine behind its registrar's messenger is gone, so it cannot guard against this itself.

### Actual results

The app crashes with an uncaught `NSInternalInconsistencyException` (in release builds too), whether iOS disconnects the scene in the background or terminates the app.

### Workaround

The app swizzles `FlutterEngine`. `destroyContext` flags the engine as torn down. On a flagged engine, `setMessageHandlerOnChannel:binaryMessageHandler:taskQueue:` returns `-1` for a non-nil handler, and `sendOnChannel:message:binaryReply:` drops the message. This depends on the private `destroyContext` selector.

### Flutter Doctor output

Flutter 3.47.5 stable (revision 6a19cca564), iOS 27.0.1. The same code is on master: `FlutterEngine.mm` `setMessageHandlerOnChannel:binaryMessageHandler:taskQueue:` and `platform_message_handler_ios.mm` `HandlePlatformMessage`.

body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

material_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock
  cupertino_ui:
    dependency: transitive
    description:
      name: cupertino_ui
      sha256: a47c4e7c66fd7444a063a602597fceb238f705c3f6b1322bc0053d0a2638ee6e
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.1.4"
  material_ui:
    dependency: "direct main"
    description:
      name: material_ui
      sha256: e4031746f96c8316864d9b92bce375f1320a36ed56e166307e1e1bda9d90b4ab
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.8.0"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter build apk --release --analyze-size --target-platform=android-arm64` with the code sample.
2. Look for `cupertino_ui/src/radio.dart` and `src/checkbox.dart` in the report.

### Expected results

Neither file, since only `Radio.adaptive` and `Checkbox.adaptive` build Cupertino controls.

### Actual results

| Build | `radio.dart` | `checkbox.dart` |
|---|---|---|
| Code sample | 8,728 B | 9,355 B |
| Without the `Radio` and `Checkbox` | none | none |

`build` picks the `.adaptive` arm from a private field (`_radioType`, `_checkboxType`), so AOT keeps it. `RadioListTile` and `CheckboxListTile` do the same.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(body: _Controls())));

class _Controls extends StatelessWidget {
  const _Controls();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => RadioGroup<int>(
    groupValue: 1,
    onChanged: (_) {},
    child: Column(
      children: [
        const Radio<int>(value: 1),
        Checkbox(value: true, onChanged: (_) {}),
      ],
    ),
  );
}
```

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

<details open><summary>Doctor output</summary>

```console

    • Framework revision 737ba8f885, 2026-10-22 21:37:31 -0700
    • Engine revision cf636b1dfb
    • Dart version 3.13.7
```

</details>

title: Refresh Focus semantics after attaching to its focus parent

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

labels.name: f: focus
labels.description: Focus traversal, gaining or losing focus

body:
Refresh Focus semantics after attaching to its focus parent

A Focus under ExcludeFocus can initially expose a focus action and a focusable semantics flag even though its FocusNode cannot request focus. The cached canRequestFocus value is read before the node is attached to its parent; reparenting can change that value without notifying the node.

Refresh the cached value after reparenting, before constructing the semantics widget. Tests cover initial exclusion, toggling exclusion, externally managed focus nodes, and moving a keyed child between excluded and permitted parents.

Fixes #195292.

Validation on Windows:
- All 199 tests in focus_scope_test.dart, focus_manager_test.dart, and focus_traversal_test.dart pass.
- All three added regression tests fail on the unchanged production code.
- The 49 focus-scope tests also pass with coverage; the new assignment is covered.
- Static analysis, Dart formatting, and git diff --check pass.

The full repository suite and interactive screen-reader/browser testing were not run. No public API or documentation migration is required.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The contributor reviewed and accepted this final diff and description before publication.

title: Fix TapGestureRecognizer stuck state when native dialog swallows pointer events

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

labels.name: f: gestures
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter/gestures repository.

body:
Fix TapGestureRecognizer stuck state when native dialog swallows pointer events

## Background

On Windows, when a native platform dialog (e.g. file picker opened via `IFileDialog` / `file_selector` package) closes after the user **confirms** (clicks "Open" / "Save"), the OS may have swallowed the pointer up/cancel events that originated from the Flutter window before the dialog appeared.

**Why clicking X to dismiss works but confirming doesn't:**
- Clicking X → dialog sends a close event → Windows forwards the pointer up back to the original window → Flutter receives it → TapGestureRecognizer completes normally → `_reset()` called → `state = ready`
- Clicking "Open" → dialog closes via native file operation → pointer events consumed by OS → Flutter window never receives pointer up/cancel → TapGestureRecognizer stuck

## Root Cause

`TapGestureRecognizer.addAllowedPointer` guards initialization with:

```dart
if (state == GestureRecognizerState.ready) {
  if (_down != null && _up != null) {
    _reset();  // Only resets when BOTH down AND up have arrived
  }
  _down = event;
}
```

When the native dialog swallowed the up event, the recognizer state is:
- `state` = `possible` (not `ready` — because arena was never resolved)
- `_down` = PointerDownEvent (pointer id = 4)
- `_up` = `null` (swallowed)
- `primaryPointer` = 4

A new user click produces pointer id 74:
1. `addAllowedPointer(74)` → `state != ready` → skip initialization → `_down` stays pointer 4
2. `acceptGesture(74)` → `74 != primaryPointer(4)` → `_checkDown()` / `_checkUp()` never fire → tap never triggers

The widget keeps receiving pointer events (hit test, listener callbacks), but the gesture recognizer state machine is permanently wedged until the widget tree is rebuilt.

## Fix

At the **top** of `addAllowedPointer`, detect the stale sequence and force-resolve it:

```dart
if (state != GestureRecognizerState.ready &&
    _down != null &&
    _down!.pointer != event.pointer) {
  resolve(GestureDisposition.rejected);
  stopTrackingPointer(_down!.pointer);
  _reset();
}
```

The normal guarded block runs afterward — `_reset()` sets `state = ready`, so the existing path handles the new pointer correctly.

### Why this is safe (no behavioral change in normal flows)

The fix only fires when **all three** conditions hold simultaneously:
1. `state != ready` — recognizer is in the middle of tracking a gesture
2. `_down != null` — a previous pointer down was recorded
3. `_down.pointer != event.pointer` — the new pointer id differs from the one being tracked

In normal gesture flows:
- Same pointer down → `_down.pointer == event.pointer` → condition 3 false → **skip**
- Same pointer up → `state` becomes `ready` after arena resolve → condition 1 false → **skip**
- Fresh gesture (all null) → `state == ready` → condition 1 false → **skip**

## Reproduction

```dart
import 'package:file_selector/file_selector.dart';

// After this, TapGestureRecognizer on the TextField/EditableText
// beneath will be stuck — click on it and the cursor won't move.
XFile? file = await openFile();
```

Tested on: Windows 11, Flutter 3.27+, file_selector 1.0+.

## Scope

- `TapGestureRecognizer` (this fix) — **Fixed**
- `DoubleTapGestureRecognizer` — Internally delegates to `TapGestureRecognizer` for the first tap, so it benefits from this fix automatically
- `PanGestureRecognizer` / `DragGestureRecognizer` / `ScaleGestureRecognizer` — Unrelated, OneSequenceGestureRecognizer has its own lifecycle handling
- Desktop only? — iOS `UIImagePickerController` / Android `Activity` intent-based pickers also involve native view transitions that can swallow pointers. Same stale-state class of bug could affect them, but only Windows has been confirmed to trigger it so far.

body:
**Once an app calls `setFlashMode`, every `takePicture()` sets the same flash mode on
`ImageCapture` again, which adds roughly 250-300 ms to each capture.** This happens
even when the mode is `FlashMode.off` and never changes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a camera with `ResolutionPreset.high`.
2. Call `setFlashMode(FlashMode.off)`.
3. Call `takePicture()` repeatedly and measure the latency.

### Results

| | ZSL off | ZSL on |
|---|---|---|
| `setFlashMode` never called | 517 ms | 360 ms |
| `setFlashMode(FlashMode.off)` called once | **794 ms** | **656 ms** |

Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N), camera_android_camerax 0.7.6, CameraX 1.6.2. Each value is
the median of 12 shots, after 2 warm-up shots, 600 ms apart. "ZSL on" means
`setZeroShutterLagEnabled(true)`.

### Why

`takePicture` calls `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` before every capture whenever a
flash mode has been set (since flutter/packages#3800). CameraX keeps the flash mode
on the `ImageCapture` instance for subsequent captures, so the repeated call does not
change anything. In CameraX 1.6.2, `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` has no check for an
unchanged mode, so each call still goes through `CameraControl.setFlashMode`. (The
androidx-main source has since added that check.)

### Proposed fix

Only call `ImageCapture.setFlashMode` in `takePicture` when the mode differs from the
one last applied to the current `ImageCapture` instance. The torch behavior from
flutter/packages#4903 (clearing a previous flash mode when torch is enabled) stays
the same.

body:
**With `ResolutionPreset.max`, zero-shutter-lag (ZSL) has no effect, so none of the
`ResolutionPreset`s gives full-resolution photos with ZSL.** The other presets work
with ZSL, but cap the photo size (`high`: 1280x720; `ultraHigh` requests 16:9 up to
3840x2160).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a camera with `ResolutionPreset.max` on a device where
   `isZeroShutterLagSupported()` returns `true`.
2. Call `setZeroShutterLagEnabled(true)`.
3. Measure `takePicture()` latency.

### Results

Every call succeeds and nothing is logged, but capture latency does not change:

| Preset | ZSL off | ZSL on |
|---|---|---|
| `ResolutionPreset.high` | 517 ms | **360 ms** |
| `ResolutionPreset.max` | 828 ms | **826 ms** |

Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N), camera_android_camerax 0.7.6, CameraX 1.6.2. Each value is
the median of 12 shots, after 2 warm-up shots, 600 ms apart.

### Why

**When ZSL is enabled after the camera is initialized, which is the only order the
`camera` package allows, CameraX keeps ZSL off if any use case prefers higher
resolution over capture rate, and `ResolutionPreset.max` sets that on every use case**
(since flutter/packages#11956).

At the platform level, requesting ZSL before `createCamera` does give ZSL with `max`
(536 ms on the same device), so the conflict only shows up when `ImageCapture` is
recreated after the other use cases are bound.

### Proposed fix

- When ZSL is enabled, `ResolutionPreset.max` uses the largest regular size for still
  capture, that is, the largest size in the normal output size list rather than the
  separate high-resolution list (`getHighResolutionOutputSizes`). Without ZSL, still
  capture with `max` is unchanged.
- `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis` with `max` no longer prefer higher resolution, with
  or without ZSL (see below).

On the Galaxy S21 this gives full-resolution photos with ZSL: 3024x4032, with the
same latency as `high` + ZSL.

### Trade-off to confirm

On devices whose largest photo size is only in the high-resolution list, enabling
ZSL with `max` gives the largest regular size instead. For the device reported in
flutter/packages#11956 that would be 3264x2448 instead of 4624x3468. CameraX does not
allow ZSL with high-resolution sizes.

### Preview and ImageAnalysis

flutter/packages#11956 first applied the high-resolution mode to `ImageCapture` only,
since the original issue was about still capture. At review request it was extended
to `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis`, so that `max` means the highest resolution across
the board.

Keeping it there would keep ZSL off. Removing it from `ImageCapture` only still gives
833 ms with ZSL enabled:

- `Preview` cannot be recreated when ZSL is enabled. Recreating it creates a new
  `SurfaceProducer` and so a new texture ID, but that ID was already returned as the
  camera ID, and the camera package only allows enabling ZSL after initialization.
- High-resolution sizes cannot sustain 20 fps (`getHighResolutionOutputSizes`), which
  streaming use cases like `Preview` and `ImageAnalysis` rely on.

On the Galaxy S21 the `max` preview is 1440x1080 with or without the mode. Is there a
use case that needs high-resolution sizes for `Preview` or `ImageAnalysis`?

title: Extract a handleThumbPressCancel hook in RawScrollbarState

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

labels.name: f: scrolling
labels.description: Viewports, list views, slivers, etc.

body:
When a touch lands inside the scrollbar thumb's padded hit test area but
outside the scrollbar track, the thumb drag gesture recognizer and the
scrollable's own drag gesture recognizer both join the gesture arena. If
the pointer is lifted before the thumb drag is accepted, the thumb drag
loses the arena and is canceled instead of ended. RawScrollbar handled
that in the private _handleThumbDragCancel, which only cleaned up the
hold/drag activities, giving subclasses no hook to undo a reaction they
started in handleThumbPress (as CupertinoScrollbar does for its thickness
animation) when the drag never gets that far.

_handleThumbDragCancel now delegates to a new protected, mustCallSuper
handleThumbPressCancel() method that subclasses can override, mirroring
the existing handleThumbPressEnd. The default implementation keeps the
previous cleanup behavior unchanged, so this is behavior preserving on
its own.

Split out of flutter/flutter#191691, which also overrides this hook in
CupertinoScrollbar to reverse its thickness animation — that is a
Cupertino change blocked by the code freeze (see #188444) and is ported
separately to flutter/packages, where the component-specific regressions remain.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/162747

Commit `09dd7c8caca` adds in-repository widget regression coverage without changing Material or Cupertino components. The new test fails when thumb-cancel dispatch bypasses the subclass hook; it also checks that a subsequent drag ends normally. title: Use the value getter instead of the cached field in FormFieldState

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

body:
FormFieldState.isValid and FormFieldState.validate() read the validator's
input from the private _value field, bypassing any override of the value
getter. A FormField subclass that overrides value to read from an external
source of truth (for example a TextEditingController) could therefore have
its validator called with a stale cached value instead of the current one,
notably when validation runs before the subclass's own listener has had a
chance to call didChange().

isValid and validate() now read through the value getter like the rest of
FormFieldState already does, so overrides are respected.

Split out of flutter/flutter#191658, which also updated TextFormField and
CupertinoTextFormFieldRow to override value — those are Material/Cupertino
changes blocked by the code freeze (see #188444) and are ported separately

title: Fix duplicate selection handle leaders on repeated paints

labels.name: framework
labels.description: flutter/packages/flutter repository. See also f: labels.

body:
A RenderParagraph can be painted more than once in the same frame. For
example RenderListWheelViewport, which backs CupertinoPicker, paints the
item that overlaps the center of the wheel twice: once clipped to the
magnifier and once clipped to the dimmed cylindrical part. Every paint of
a selected _SelectableFragment pushed a brand new LeaderLayer for the
selection handle LayerLinks, so a double paint left each link with two
leaders and tripped the _debugPreviousLeaders!.isEmpty assertion of
LayerLink at the end of the frame.

_SelectableFragment now keeps a LayerHandle for each handle leader layer
it pushes. The layer tree below a repaint boundary is torn down before it
is repainted, so a leader layer that is still attached can only come from
an earlier paint of the current frame. In that case the handle layer is
already in the tree and pushing another one is skipped.

Split out of flutter/flutter#191677, which also added a CupertinoPicker
regression test — that is a Cupertino change blocked by the code freeze
(see #188444) and is ported separately to flutter/packages. This PR now
also includes a rendering-only regression in `paragraph_test.dart`: it
paints a selected paragraph twice, checks that both handle leaders are
reused, rebuilds the layer tree, and checks handle-link cleanup.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/140543

## Test plan

- Complete `test/rendering/paragraph_test.dart`: 48 tests passed, including the repeated-paint regression.
- Targeted `dart analyze --fatal-infos` and formatter check: passed.
- Mutation check: disabling the attached-leader guard makes the new test fail because a duplicate leader replaces the original; restored guard passes.
- Validation used cached engine artifacts `773d8b3b068886a279acc1e3f23ce4710bbaac72`; the engine source tree is identical to the already-validated draft using those artifacts.
- Full repository suites and real-device/platform integration were not run. The draft remains subject to contributor review and maintainer CI/review gates.
- Signed replacement: the complete contribution from https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/191713 is preserved in GitHub-verified commit `7bd407ca7803d5ca1731a39b988c205679967d44` (`verified: true`, `reason: valid`). The original coverage commit `1fa4b6191ec838ba05ce112925735010138acb72` was unsigned; its branch/history remain unchanged. The new branch starts at the original PR merge-base `d79b030de22d286f21162b08ce35df244e3f1ae7` with one signed snapshot commit, not the original unsigned feature commits.
- Historical validation above ran on original head `1fa4b6191ec838ba05ce112925735010138acb72`, tree `56912db7347354b6d642ec196d0ef5117f99bf12`. GitHub confirms the replacement commit has exactly that same full tree. These are retained test results on identical contents, not newly run tests, current-head CI results, or human verification. title: [iOS][UIScene] Plugins receive application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: twice on a cold launch with connection options (background_fetch crashes)

labels.name: waiting for response
labels.description: The Flutter team cannot make further progress on this issue until the original reporter responds

body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Take an iOS app on Flutter 3.44.1 that has adopted the UIScene lifecycle (`UIApplicationSceneManifest` in Info.plist, `UISceneDelegateClassName` = `FlutterSceneDelegate` or a subclass; plugins registered from `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine`).
2. Add a plugin that still uses the application lifecycle (no `FlutterSceneLifeCycleDelegate`) and does something that must happen exactly once in `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:`. The real-world case is `background_fetch` (Transistorsoft), which registers its `BGTaskScheduler` launch handler there. A minimal stand-in is a `FlutterApplicationLifeCycleDelegate` that counts calls (see code sample).
3. Terminate the app.
4. Cold-launch it through something that carries **scene connection options**: tap a local/push notification, a Live Activity, a Home Screen quick action, or open a custom URL scheme (`xcrun simctl openurl <udid> myscheme://x` reproduces it on the simulator).

Launching from the app icon (no connection options) does not reproduce.

### Expected results

Plugins receive `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:` once per process, as they do under the classic app-delegate lifecycle.

### Actual results

Plugins receive it **twice** within the same launch:

1. From the storyboard `FlutterViewController` init: `sceneFallbackWillFinishLaunchingApplication:` / `sceneFallbackDidFinishLaunchingApplication:` ([FlutterViewController.mm#L321-L324](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterViewController.mm#L321-L324)). This sets `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch = YES` ([FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L121-L129](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L121-L129)).
2. Again from `scene:willConnectToSession:options:` when no plugin claims the connection: `FlutterPluginSceneLifeCycleDelegate` calls `sceneWillConnectFallback:` ([FlutterSceneLifeCycle.mm#L263-L270](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterSceneLifeCycle.mm#L263-L270)), which converts the connection options to launch options and calls `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:isFallbackForScene:YES` directly, **without checking `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch`** ([FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L156-L173](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/710263041fe6f956e7a328756c63d751cd27f98a/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate.mm#L156-L173)). Its own guard (`_sceneWillConnectFallbackCalled`) only prevents a third call; it does not know about the first one.

The only difference between the two deliveries is the `launchOptions` dictionary (empty the first time, the converted connection options the second time), so a plugin cannot tell them apart.

With `background_fetch` the second call ends the process in under a second:

```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInternalInconsistencyException',
reason: 'Launch handler for task with identifier com.transistorsoft.fetch has already been registered'

-[BGTaskScheduler registerForTaskWithIdentifier:usingQueue:launchHandler:]
-[TSBackgroundFetch registerAppRefreshTask]
-[TSBackgroundFetch didFinishLaunching]
-[BackgroundFetchPlugin application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:]
-[FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:isFallbackForScene:]
-[FlutterPluginAppLifeCycleDelegate sceneWillConnectFallback:]
-[FlutterPluginSceneLifeCycleDelegate scene:willConnectToSession:flutterEngine:options:]
-[FlutterSceneDelegate scene:willConnectToSession:options:]
```

Seen in production on iOS 18 through iOS 27 (same engine, so the OS version does not matter); 100% of launches from a Live Activity / notification tap crashed, while icon launches were fine, which is why it passed QA. The code paths above are unchanged on `master` at 7102630 as of 2026-10-27.

Workaround that works for us: register a tiny `FlutterSceneLifeCycleDelegate` through `registrar.addSceneDelegate(...)` whose `scene(_:willConnectTo:options:)` returns `true`. Because a plugin then "handled" the connection, the engine skips `sceneWillConnectFallback:`. That is only acceptable when the app consumes its URL / notification / shortcut itself via the scene delegate; otherwise legacy plugins lose the launch options.

Suggested fix: make `sceneWillConnectFallback:` respect `didForwardApplicationDidLaunch` (or merge the two fallbacks so the converted connection options are passed in the single delivery). Related readability issue: #185705.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

A lifecycle delegate that shows the double delivery without any third-party plugin. Register it from `didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine` (so it exists before the storyboard `FlutterViewController` is created), then cold-launch via a URL scheme or notification tap.

```swift
final class LaunchCounter: NSObject, FlutterApplicationLifeCycleDelegate {
  private var count = 0
  func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                   didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
    count += 1
    print("didFinishLaunching delivered \(count)x, options: \(launchOptions.keys)")
    precondition(count == 1, "didFinishLaunching delivered twice")   // trips on the second delivery
    return true
  }
}

// in AppDelegate (FlutterAppDelegate subclass, UIScene manifest present)
func didInitializeImplicitFlutterEngine(_ engineBridge: FlutterImplicitEngineBridge) {
  GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register(with: engineBridge.pluginRegistry)
  engineBridge.pluginRegistry.registrar(forPlugin: "LaunchCounter")?
    .addApplicationDelegate(LaunchCounter())
}
```

Output on a tap/URL cold launch:

```
didFinishLaunching delivered 1x, options: []
didFinishLaunching delivered 2x, options: [UIApplicationLaunchOptionsKey(_rawValue: UIApplicationLaunchOptionsURLKey), ...]
```

</details>

title: [a11y] Keep AccessibilityBridge usable after nested reparenting

labels.name: engine
labels.description: flutter/engine related. See also e: labels.

labels.name: a: accessibility
labels.description: Accessibility, e.g. VoiceOver or TalkBack. (aka a11y)

body:
A single semantics update can insert a new node above an existing subtree and, in the same update, move a node out of that subtree. For example, `0->1->2->3->4` becomes `0->1->11->{2->3, 12->4}`: new node 11 adopts 2, and 4 moves from 3 to new node 12.

`AccessibilityBridge::CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate` emits its removal entries in `unordered_map` order. If the entry for the outer parent (1) comes before the entry for the inner parent (3), `ui::AXTree::Unserialize` rejects the update:

```
Failed to update ui::AXTree, error: 3 will not be in the tree and is not the new root
```

Removing 2 from 1 already deletes 3, so the later entry for 3 is invalid. `CommitUpdates` then returns without clearing `pending_semantics_node_updates_`. It also checks `tree_->error()`, which `ui::AXTree` never resets, so every later `CommitUpdates` takes the error path as well: accessibility events stop, later reparenting updates are cut off after the removal step, and stale entries pile up. In release builds this ends in two crashes:

* Once a child id is listed under both a stale pending parent and its new parent, the second `std::find` in `CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate` misses, and `child_ids.erase(end())` corrupts the heap (the `assert` is compiled out).
* `SemanticsNode::flags` points into the embedder's `FlutterSemanticsUpdate2`, which is freed after the callback. A stale entry that is never overwritten reads freed memory in `SetRoleFromFlutterUpdate` and the other `Set*FromFlutterUpdate` methods.

We see both in field crash reports from a Windows release app (3.47.7) with an MSAA client attached. The x64 stacks end in the `erase` in `CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate`, called from `CommitUpdates`; an arm64 stack ends in `SetRoleFromFlutterUpdate` reading `flags->is_button`.

This PR:

* Emits the removal entries deepest parent first, so the removal update is valid in any hash order. This is the actual fix for the rejected update.
* Checks the return value of `Unserialize` instead of the sticky `tree_->error()`, so a rejected update no longer breaks every later update.
* Clears both pending maps when the removal update is rejected, matching what `CommitUpdates` already does when the second update is rejected.
* Erases a child id only if it is still in the parent's `child_ids`.
* Copies `FlutterSemanticsFlags` into `SemanticsNode` instead of storing the `flags2` pointer. It was the only pointer `SemanticsNode` kept into the update buffer; strings, children and custom action ids were already copied.

With the ordering fix, the removal update cannot be rejected for well-formed input; the remaining changes are hardening.

This complements #190903, which guards the null-parent dereference a few lines earlier in the same function and does not cover the cases above. The two changes touch different lines. I ran `accessibility_bridge_unittests.cc` in a standalone CMake build (MSVC, and clang with libc++); #190903's patch applies cleanly on top and all tests from both pass there. I did not run a full GN engine build.

Tests added to `accessibility_bridge_unittests.cc`:

* `CanReparentNodeInsideReparentedSubtree` applies the transition above, adding the two moves in both orders because the outcome depends on hash map order. It checks the resulting tree and that a later update is still applied. Without the fix it fails: an `assert` in debug builds, and in release builds node 11 is missing and the error above is logged.
* `AppliesUpdatesAfterRejectedUpdate` commits an invalid update (a child that does not exist), then a valid reparenting update, and checks that the valid one is applied and emits events. Without the fix the moved node is missing and no events are sent.
* `CopiesSemanticsFlags` changes the caller's flags after `AddFlutterSemanticsNodeUpdate` and before `CommitUpdates`. Without the fix the role follows the changed flags.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/175041

title: [VPAT] Expose a semantics text field value while it is not being edited

labels.name: a: text input

labels.name: engine

labels.name: a: accessibility
labels.description: Accessibility, e.g. VoiceOver or TalkBack. (aka a11y)

labels.name: platform-web
labels.description: Web applications specifically

labels.name: will affect goldens
labels.description: Changes to golden files

labels.name: team-web
labels.description: Owned by Web platform team

labels.name: CICD
labels.description: Run CI/CD

body:
Fixes #147200

## Problem
With semantics enabled, a text field's `<input>` only gets a value while it is focused, because only the text editing strategy writes it. A field that was never focused, such as a disabled field showing prefilled text, exposes an empty value, so screen readers do not read its content. Two tests pinned this with a TODO pointing at #147200.

## Fix
`SemanticTextField` now copies the semantics value into its element when the value changes and the field is not being edited. The active field is left to the text editing strategy, obscured fields are skipped because their semantics value is masked, and fields owned by an autofill group are skipped. The two tests now check the real value, and new tests cover disabled, multi-line, obscured, autofill-owned and updated values.

## Demo
Open the a11y_assessments text field page with semantics enabled and move a screen reader to the second, disabled "Email" field.

Before: VoiceOver says "Email, dimmed, edit text" and never says "xyz". The element's `value` is empty.
After: VoiceOver also reads "xyz", and the element has `value="xyz"`.

Console check: `[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-semantics-role="text-field"]')].map(e => e.value)` returns `["", ""]` before and `["", "xyz"]` after.
