title: [web] iOS Safari: Japanese IME duplicates composed text in a TextField with enableInteractiveSelection: false

labels.name: a: text input
labels.description: Entering text in a text field or keyboard related problems

labels.name: platform-web
labels.description: Web applications specifically

labels.name: has reproducible steps
labels.description: The issue has been confirmed reproducible and is ready to work on

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Important issues not at the top of the work list

labels.name: team-text-input
labels.description: Owned by Text Input team

body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the code sample below for the web and open it in Safari on iOS.
2. Add the Japanese Kana keyboard (Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards > Add New Keyboard > Japanese > Kana) and switch to it with the globe key.
3. Tap the "selection off" field. On the 12-key Kana layout, tap は, tap な, then choose the candidate 花.
4. Do the same in the "default" field and in the "selection off, single-line" field.

Reproduced on the iPhone 17 Simulator, iOS 27.0, Safari 27.0, with a debug web build on Flutter 3.47.7 stable. The same duplication also showed up in a Flutter web app that uses `enableInteractiveSelection: false`, on the iOS 18.6 Simulator (Safari 18.6) and on a real iPhone (iOS 18.7.1, Safari). Desktop Safari was not tested.

### Expected results

Every field composes in place, as the default field does: は, then はな, then 花.

### Actual results

The two "selection off" fields set `enableInteractiveSelection: false`.

| Field                              | after は | after な | after 花 |
|------------------------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| selection off (textarea)           | は       | ははな   | ははな花 |
| default (textarea)                 | は       | はな     | 花       |
| selection off, single-line (input) | は       | ははな   | ははな花 |

Each key after the first re-inserts the whole preedit at the caret, and choosing the candidate appends it instead of replacing the preedit. The field keeps the duplicated text: the hidden DOM element and the rendered field both end with ははな花.

---

**Cause**

On iOS Safari, `IOSTextEditingStrategy` routes the hidden element's `input` event and the document's `selectionchange` to `DefaultTextEditingStrategy.handleChange`, which first calls `suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`. When `enableInteractiveSelection` is false and the DOM selection is not collapsed, that function collapses the selection to its end and writes it back with `EditingState.applyToDomElement` (`value = text`, then `setSelectionRange`). The write happens synchronously inside the event, and nothing checks for an active composition.

WebKit dispatches each `insertCompositionText` input event while the selection spans the marked text (`[0,1]`, `[1,3]` and `[3,4]` in the log below). The engine collapses that selection during the event. After that, WebKit no longer treats the text as marked, but it never fires `compositionend`. The next key therefore starts a new composition at the caret with the whole preedit as its data, and the candidate arrives as one more composition inserted at the caret.

- 3.47.7: [`handleChange`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1617-L1642), [`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1644-L1660), [`EditingState.applyToDomElement`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1065-L1079)
- main (aebd23e2d4): [`handleChange`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1800-L1825), [`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1827-L1843), [`EditingState.applyToDomElement`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1191-L1205). The function is unchanged on main.

`suppressInteractiveSelectionIfNeeded` was added in #171935, which first shipped in 3.35.0. I have not bisected this.

**Suggested fix**

Skip the DOM write while a composition is active, but still return the collapsed state to the framework. This is the same approach as the existing guard in `updateElementPlacement`, which skips `placeElement()` while `composingText != null` (#98817, fixed by flutter/engine#51323; [3.47.7](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.7/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1541-L1555), [main](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/aebd23e2d4d345c1b2fecccccd9df91daea1c17f/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1713-L1727)):

```dart
    final EditingState newEditingState = editingState.copyWith(
      baseOffset: editingState.extentOffset,
      extentOffset: editingState.extentOffset,
    );
    // Writing the DOM selection mid-composition makes WebKit drop the
    // composition without a compositionend. See also #98817.
    if (composingText == null) {
      newEditingState.applyToDomElement(activeDomElement);
    }
    return newEditingState;
```

`compositionupdate` sets `composingText` before the `input` event, so the check covers both the `input` and the `selectionchange` paths. `InputEvent.isComposing` would cover only `input`. I have not tested this patch.

This is related to #193847 (fixed by #194096) but is a different bug: that one is a stale composing range after the framework rewrites the text in the middle of a composition.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// Repro: iOS Safari + Japanese Kana keyboard duplicates composed text in a
// TextField with enableInteractiveSelection: false. Compose は, な, then 花.
void main() => runApp(const ReproApp());

class ReproApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const ReproApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: SafeArea(
          child: Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.all(16),
            child: Column(
              children: [
                TextField(
                  enableInteractiveSelection: false,
                  maxLines: null,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'selection off'),
                ),
                SizedBox(height: 16),
                TextField(
                  maxLines: null,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'default'),
                ),
                SizedBox(height: 16),
                TextField(
                  enableInteractiveSelection: false,
```

body:
### Help us understand the severity of this issue

- [ ] causing severe production issues e.g. malfunctions or data loss
- [ ] blocking next binary release
- [x] blocking a client feature launch within a quarter
- [ ] nice-to-have but does not block a launch within the next quarter

### Steps to reproduce

Enable Talkback
1. Using swipe forward gesture, swipe through the list.
2. When you reach the end of the list, swipe backwards through the list

### Expected results

The previous list item should be focused when moving focus backwards.

### Actual results

Rather than focusing the direct-previous list item, the list instead scrolls all the way up, with the focus ring dropping down with the item that was focused previously until the list scrolls all the way up and the focus ring moves to the top item.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const MaterialApp(home: TalkBackBackwardSkipRepro()));
}

class TalkBackBackwardSkipRepro extends StatelessWidget {
  const TalkBackBackwardSkipRepro({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('TalkBack Backward Skip Repro')),
      body: Center(
        child: DecoratedBox(
          decoration: BoxDecoration(border: Border.all()),
          child: SizedBox(
            height: 100,
            width: 360,
            child: ListView(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: 76, bottom: 20),
              children: [
                for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) ...[
                  SizedBox(
                    height: 56,
                    child: ListTile(
                      title: Text('Row $i'),
                      trailing: IconButton(
                        icon: const Icon(Icons.more_vert),
                        tooltip: 'Row $i options',
                        onPressed: () {},
                      ),
                      onTap: () {},
                    ),
                  ),
                  if (i < 5) const SizedBox(height: 28),
                ],
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Flutter app with a full-screen `AndroidView` (an `EagerGestureRecognizer` is set, so every pointer is forwarded).
2. In the native view, log every `MotionEvent` with its pointer ids, and flag events that are impossible given the earlier ones (e.g. `ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for an id that is already down).
3. On a physical device, keep one finger down and repeatedly lift one finger while landing another at nearly the same moment (a "drumming" motion with 2–3 extra fingers).

In our test, 3 out of 8 such gestures produced an invalid stream within ~30 seconds.

### Expected results

The platform view receives a consistent pointer stream, as it would when hosted natively: each pointer id goes down once, keeps its id until it goes up, and every `MOVE` contains exactly the pointers that are down.

```console
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1]     t=15800488
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 2]     t=15800488
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800638
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_UP(2)   ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800688
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1]
```

### Actual results

The same finger is reported under different ids. The platform view receives `ACTION_POINTER_DOWN` for an id that is already down, `ACTION_POINTER_UP` for an id that never went down, and `MOVE` events whose pointer set changes without any down/up event:

```console
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1]     t=15800488
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(1) ids=[0, 2]     t=15800488
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_DOWN(2) ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800638   <- id 2 is already down
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1, 2]
ACTION_POINTER_UP(1)   ids=[0, 1, 2]  t=15800688   <- lifts id 1, but the finger that lifted is id 2
ACTION_MOVE            ids=[0, 1]                  <- id 2 disappears, id 1 stays
```

Native gesture code that tracks pointers by id breaks on this stream. For example, [mapbox-gestures-android](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gestures-android) throws `IllegalArgumentException: invalid pointerIndex -1` and `NullPointerException` ([mapbox/mapbox-maps-flutter#1146](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-maps-flutter/issues/1146)), and those exceptions reach Dart as unhandled `PlatformException`s from `AndroidViewController.sendMotionEvent`.

#### Cause

Two id assignments are mixed in the stream the platform view receives:

1. **Dart assigns its own Android pointer ids.** `_AndroidMotionEventConverter.handlePointerDownEvent` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/platform_views.dart`) gives each new pointer the lowest id that is not in `usedAndroidPointerIds`, and frees an id as soon as it handles the pointer up. Android keeps the id of a lifted pointer reserved until the end of the input frame in which it lifted. So when a finger lifts and another lands in the **same frame**, Android gives the new finger a fresh id (2), but Dart reuses the id it just freed (1). From then on, Dart's ids and Android's ids for the same finger differ.

2. **The engine sends a mix of original and rebuilt events.** `PlatformViewsController.toMotionEvent` returns the original Android `MotionEvent` (with Android's ids) when its pointer count and action match the framework's event. Otherwise it rebuilds the event from the framework's pointer properties (with Dart's ids). This was added in #178528 (the fix for #176574). The check compares only the pointer count and action, not the pointer ids.

When the ids have diverged, `MOVE` events usually match and pass through with Android's ids. `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` events often don't, because Dart orders pointers by insertion and Android orders them by id, so the action index differs. Those events are rebuilt with Dart's ids. The platform view gets both kinds of event, so a finger's id appears to change.

Framework-side trace of the same moment (debug prints added locally to `_AndroidMotionEventConverter`; `androidId` is decoded from `event.device`):

```console
free   pointer=18 dartId=1 used={0, 1}                                t=15800488
assign pointer=19 androidId=2 dartId=1 used={0, 1}                    t=15800488  <- same frame: Android picks 2, Dart reuses 1
...
assign pointer=20 androidId=1 dartId=2 used={0, 1, 2}                t=15800638  <- Android reuses 1, Dart picks 2
send   _TransformedPointerDownEvent action=517 dartIds=[0, 1, 2]                  <- action index differs, so the engine rebuilds it with Dart's ids
```

Possible fixes: have `_AndroidMotionEventConverter` use Android's pointer id (it is already available in `PointerEvent.device`) instead of assigning its own, or have `toMotionEvent` compare pointer ids as well before reusing the original event.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/gestures.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: ReproPage()));

class ReproPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const ReproPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      body: AndroidView(
        viewType: 'touch-checker',
        layoutDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
        creationParamsCodec: const StandardMessageCodec(),
        gestureRecognizers: <Factory<OneSequenceGestureRecognizer>>{
          Factory<OneSequenceGestureRecognizer>(() => EagerGestureRecognizer()),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

```kotlin
class TouchCheckerView(context: Context) : View(context) {
  private val downIds = mutableSetOf<Int>()

  override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
    val ids = (0 until event.pointerCount).map { event.getPointerId(it) }
    val actionId = event.getPointerId(event.actionIndex)
    Log.d(TAG, "${MotionEvent.actionToString(event.action)} ids=$ids t=${event.eventTime}")

    val expected = when (event.actionMasked) {
      MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> downIds + actionId
      else -> downIds.toSet()
    }
    when {
      event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN && actionId in downIds ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: POINTER_DOWN for id $actionId, which is already down $downIds")
      event.actionMasked == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP && actionId !in downIds ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: POINTER_UP for id $actionId, which is not down $downIds")
      event.actionMasked != MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL && ids.toSet() != expected ->
        Log.e(TAG, "INCONSISTENT: event has ids $ids, expected $expected")
    }

    when (event.actionMasked) {
      MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> { downIds.clear(); downIds += actionId }
      MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> downIds += actionId
      MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP -> downIds -= actionId
      MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL -> downIds.clear()
    }
    return true
  }
}
```
